correctness.rationale: For the entire five-vertex K_{2,3} graph, the proof reduces both nonlinear norm claims to 4500 legal uncentered averaging matrices. The top Gram eigenvalue of the unique winning matrix is (8+sqrt55)/9, with simple positive eigenvector (1,1,(sqrt55-7)/3,(sqrt55-7)/3,(sqrt55-7)/3). Exact integer Bareiss/Sylvester determinants prove strict squared-norm bounds <171/100 for all 4499 alternatives; the winner exceeds 171/100. Its averaging balls are centered at each output vertex, so the centered norm equals the uncentered norm. Extrema and sign freedom follow from strict selector uniqueness and spectral simplicity. The packaged verifier was executed, and the charpoly/eigenvector identity was checked separately in exact symbolic algebra.

value.rationale: K2,3 is the unique first irregular two-connected bipartite graph; minimum degree two on its 2+3 bipartition forces all cross edges. It naturally tests whether enlarging from centered to uncentered graph balls changes exact Hilbert amplification as it does on some paths. The equality of the two sharp norms, a closed radical value, and a single automorphism-fixed nonnegative extremizing ray together give a nontrivial exact benchmark for the larger Kp,q problem. No theorem for arbitrary p,q is asserted.
